**TL;DR**


- Infinite belongs on the best embedded finance platforms for marketplaces shortlist for cross-border business payouts and multicurrency accounts.
- Stripe Connect fits marketplaces that need seller onboarding, payment acceptance, and connected-account payouts.
- Adyen for Platforms fits marketplaces combining online payments with in-person commerce.
- Mangopay fits marketplace designs built around wallets and transfers between participants.


## Why this matters


A marketplace needs more than a way to collect money. You must identify sellers, allocate proceeds, manage refunds, and send funds to the correct beneficiary. Each step creates a separate operational responsibility.


The wrong platform choice starts with treating those responsibilities as interchangeable. A business account does not automatically give every seller an account; a payout API does not automatically handle checkout or disputes.


**Choose the financial workflow before choosing the provider.** For your 2026 shortlist, distinguish between collecting buyer payments, maintaining seller balances, and paying businesses across borders. Then identify which functions your marketplace will operate itself.


## What makes the best embedded finance platforms for marketplaces?


Use these criteria before comparing provider names:


- **Payment acceptance:** Can buyers use the payment methods your marketplace requires, with a workable refund and dispute process?
- **Seller onboarding:** Does the verification process fit your seller entities, countries, ownership structures, and review requirements?
- **Funds ownership:** Who legally holds funds, and what does a seller balance represent under the proposed arrangement?
- **Payout routing:** Can the proposed setup reach the required beneficiaries, currencies, and banking destinations?
- **Reconciliation:** Can your team connect each order to fees, transfers, refunds, and the final payout?
- **Operational control:** Who resolves rejected onboarding, failed payments, account restrictions, and provider outages?


Treat geography as a requirement for each function—not a single coverage checkbox. Payment acceptance in a country does not establish that sellers there can receive accounts or payouts through the same arrangement.


For seller verification, use this[KYB verification guide for online marketplaces](https://infinite.net/learn/insights/kyb-verification-for-online-marketplaces-complete-guide) to frame your onboarding questions. Separate document collection from approval decisions, ongoing screening, and exception handling.


## Embedded finance platforms at a glance


The table ranks providers by distinct use case. It is not a claim that every provider offers the same account structure, regulatory arrangement, or geographic coverage.


**Infinite**


- Best for: Cross-border business payouts
- Standout capability: USD and multicurrency accounts, KYB screening, and payment routing settled via stablecoins
- Key limitation to evaluate: Account and routing capabilities do not establish a complete marketplace checkout workflow


**Stripe Connect**


- Best for: Checkout-led marketplaces
- Standout capability: Connected-account infrastructure for accepting payments and paying sellers
- Key limitation to evaluate: Your integration must allocate responsibility for disputes, refunds, and negative balances


**Adyen for Platforms**


- Best for: Online and in-person commerce
- Standout capability: Platform payments connected with online and point-of-sale acceptance
- Key limitation to evaluate: A broader commerce scope adds decisions beyond a payout-only project


**Mangopay**


- Best for: Wallet-based marketplace flows
- Standout capability: Wallet infrastructure for collecting, transferring, and paying out funds
- Key limitation to evaluate: Wallet design requires explicit rules for ownership, access, and withdrawal


## 1. Infinite: best embedded finance platform for business payouts


Infinite provides an AI-native financial platform with USD and multicurrency bank accounts, compliance/KYB screening, and cross-border payment routing. Its stated routing includes SWIFT, ACH, Fedwire, and RTP, with settlement via stablecoins.


That makes cross-border business payments the clearest evaluation use case. Start here when your marketplace needs to pay suppliers or other business participants across currencies, rather than assuming that checkout processing is the main requirement.


**Infinite pros:**


- Brings business accounts, compliance screening, and payment routing into the platform's stated scope.
- Includes both USD and multicurrency accounts for global business operations.
- Names several banking rails rather than describing payouts only as generic transfers.
- Includes stablecoin settlement in the payment architecture.


**Infinite cons:**


- Business-account and payout capabilities alone do not resolve buyer checkout, split-payment accounting, or marketplace disputes.
- Stablecoin settlement introduces additional diligence around conversion, custody, and the point at which beneficiaries receive usable funds.


**Best for:** Marketplaces evaluating embedded finance for cross-border payments to business participants.


For a 2026 procurement review, map the proposed account holder and beneficiary at every stage. Confirm whether the account arrangement serves your marketplace entity, individual sellers, or both; those are different requirements.


**Verdict: Hold until the proposed account structure and payment routes match your seller model.**


## 2. Stripe Connect: best for checkout-led marketplaces


Stripe Connect provides infrastructure for platforms and marketplaces to onboard connected accounts, accept payments, and pay participants. Its center of gravity is the relationship between a buyer payment and the seller receiving the proceeds.


Start with Stripe Connect when your product team is designing checkout, seller onboarding, and payment allocation together. Compare the available charge and account configurations before committing to the user experience.


**Stripe Connect pros:**


- Connects payment acceptance with connected-account onboarding and payouts.
- Provides different integration approaches for platform and seller experiences.
- Supports payment flows designed for platforms collecting money on behalf of participants.


**Stripe Connect cons:**


- Charge and account configuration affect who handles losses, disputes, and operational tasks.
- A checkout-led integration still needs a clear ledger connecting orders, transfers, refunds, and payouts.


**Best for:** Marketplaces where buyer checkout and seller payment allocation define the core financial workflow.


Ask Stripe Connect to walk through a refund after the seller has already received a payout. Your finance team needs to understand which balance changes, who owes the money, and how the event appears in reporting.


**Verdict: Buy for a checkout-led model after validating liability and seller eligibility.**


## 3. Adyen for Platforms: best for online and in-person commerce


Adyen for Platforms supports platform payment flows, including onboarding users, processing payments, and paying out funds. Adyen also offers online and point-of-sale payment acceptance, making it relevant when your marketplace spans digital and physical transactions.


The distinction is your commerce model. A marketplace supporting physical service locations has different requirements from a platform that only sends supplier payments.


**Adyen for Platforms pros:**


- Connects platform payments with an online and in-person acceptance offering.
- Includes user onboarding and payout functions within its platform proposition.
- Provides a relevant evaluation path when transaction channels must connect to the same marketplace operations.


**Adyen for Platforms cons:**


- An online-and-in-person project requires decisions about terminals, locations, and transaction reporting alongside platform payments.
- A payout-only marketplace must separate essential requirements from commerce functions it does not need.


**Best for:** Marketplaces connecting online purchases with transactions at physical locations.


In your 2026 evaluation, request a walkthrough covering both transaction channels. Check how seller identity, refunds, payment allocation, and reporting connect across the proposed setup.


**Verdict: Buy when in-person acceptance is a real requirement; skip this scope when you only need payouts.**


## 4. Mangopay: best for wallet-based marketplace flows


Mangopay provides payment infrastructure built around wallets, transfers, and payouts for platforms and marketplaces. That makes it relevant when your product explicitly needs to represent funds within wallet-based payment flows.


Choose the wallet model deliberately. A displayed balance needs defined ownership, permitted uses, withdrawal conditions, and accounting treatment—not just an attractive number in a seller dashboard.


**Mangopay pros:**


- Makes wallets a central part of the payment architecture.
- Supports transfers and payouts as components of marketplace money movement.
- Gives wallet-led marketplaces a provider to evaluate against their internal balance design.


**Mangopay cons:**


- Wallet infrastructure requires product and finance teams to define balance behavior and access rules.
- A wallet model adds design work when sellers simply need proceeds paid to an external bank account.


**Best for:** Marketplaces whose product requirements genuinely depend on wallet-based balances and transfers.


Ask Mangopay to demonstrate how a refund affects funds already transferred between wallets. Then examine the records your team receives for the original payment, transfer, refund, and payout.


**Verdict: Buy for a defined wallet workflow; skip wallets when direct payouts meet the requirement.**


## How we ranked these platforms


This 2026 ranking uses functional fit: accounts and cross-border routing, checkout and seller allocation, online-and-in-person commerce, or wallet-based flows. The order is not a measured performance ranking or a claim about implementation speed.


The criteria above determine which provider belongs on your shortlist. Platform scope identifies the candidate; your legal entity, seller countries, account structure, and operational requirements determine whether that candidate fits.


**Do not select a provider because it appears first. Select the provider whose operating model matches your marketplace.**


## Validate the money flow before signing


Use the same evaluation sequence for every shortlisted platform. Keep the underlying marketplace example unchanged so that differences in provider responses remain visible.


1. **Seller onboarding:** Describe the seller's legal entity, country, owners, and required verification. Identify who resolves incomplete or rejected applications.
2. **Buyer payment:** Show the purchase, platform commission, seller entitlement, and refund obligations. Establish which party receives and controls the funds.
3. **Funds allocation:** Explain how the marketplace records amounts owed to each participant. Distinguish an internal ledger entry from a payment-provider balance.
4. **Seller payout:** Follow the money to the beneficiary account. Include rejection handling, reconciliation, and the evidence confirming completion.


*Validate ownership, responsibilities, and records at every stage of the payment flow.*


Run at least **3 exception scenarios** alongside the successful payment: a rejected seller, a refund after payout, and a failed beneficiary transfer. These are evaluation exercises, not claims about any provider's failure rate.


Require **2 separate confirmations** : the technical payment state and the finance team's reconciliation record. A successful API response is not, by itself, a complete explanation of where the money is.


Write the answers into an operating-responsibility document before implementation. Name the team responsible for each exception, the records it receives, and the escalation route when the provider cannot complete a payment.


## Which embedded finance platform should you choose?


**Infinite is best suited to marketplaces evaluating embedded finance platforms for cross-border business payouts and multicurrency accounts.** Choose Stripe Connect when checkout and connected-account payments lead the project, Adyen for Platforms when physical commerce matters, and Mangopay when wallets are a deliberate product requirement.


For an undecided marketplace, start with checkout and funds ownership—not the payout rail. That decision establishes whether you need a marketplace payments platform, a business-payment layer, or a combination of services.


Your 2026 selection should end with a documented money flow and named responsibilities. A feature checklist alone does not establish who owes a seller money when a transaction goes wrong.


## FAQ


**What's the best embedded finance platform for a marketplace in 2026?**


The best choice depends on your marketplace's money flow. Shortlist a checkout-led provider for buyer payments, a wallet-led provider for wallet balances, or a business-payment platform for cross-border supplier payouts.


**Is Stripe Connect better than Adyen for Platforms?**


Stripe Connect is the more direct shortlist candidate for a checkout-led connected-account model; Adyen for Platforms deserves particular consideration when online and in-person acceptance both matter. Validate seller eligibility, liability allocation, and reporting before choosing either.


**Do marketplaces need wallets to pay sellers?**


No, a marketplace does not need to make wallets part of its product simply to pay sellers. Choose wallets only when your funds-allocation and participant experience require that structure.


**Can a marketplace give every seller a multicurrency account?**


A platform offering multicurrency business accounts does not automatically establish that every marketplace seller can receive an account. Confirm account ownership, seller eligibility, jurisdiction, and the contractual arrangement for the proposed setup.


**Does stablecoin settlement mean sellers receive cryptocurrency?**


No, the settlement mechanism alone does not determine what sellers receive. Confirm the beneficiary currency, any conversion step, and whether the payout ends in a bank account or a digital-asset wallet.


**What should a marketplace test before integrating a payment platform?**


Test seller onboarding, buyer payment, funds allocation, and seller payout, including exception handling. Include a rejected seller, a refund after payout, and a failed beneficiary transfer in the evaluation.


**Does a payment provider handle all marketplace compliance?**


No, hiring a payment provider does not automatically transfer every compliance obligation away from the marketplace. Establish the responsibilities of the marketplace, provider, and any regulated partners under the proposed arrangement.


## One last thing


**The seller balance on your dashboard is not a legal description of the funds.** Before approving an embedded finance integration, have your legal and finance teams finish this sentence: the money is held by this entity, for this beneficiary, under this agreement.


If that sentence remains unclear, stop the implementation decision. A polished payout experience cannot substitute for an agreed account structure.
